pr_title: fix(pricing): price list prices perf issues

comments.body: hashPrice now emits a `min:` / `max:` / `ps:` part only when the key is present (`"min_quantity" in price`, line 1826; `"price_set_id" in price`, line 1820). The old code always emitted these keys with null. Existing rows loaded from the DB always have the key (`models/price.ts:12-13` defines min_quantity/max_quantity as nullable), so `existingPricesMap` (line 908) keys them as `...|min:|max:|...`. An incoming update without min_quantity/max_quantity (or without price_set_id) at line 962 hashes without those parts, so it misses the map. `existing` is then undefined, `entry.id` stays unset (line 979-983 path), and `upsertWithReplace` in updatePriceListPrices_ (around line 1545) inserts a new price row instead of updating the existing one. Concrete case: updatePriceListPrices with `{ price_list_id, prices: [{ currency_code: "EUR", amount: 200, price_set_id }] }` against an existing EUR price with no min/max. The old hash matched; the new one does not, which produces a duplicate EUR price in the list. The existing test passes only because it supplies the price `id`, which bypasses the hash lookup.

In addPrices_, when no input price has an id or a constraint (for example `addPrices([{ priceSetId, prices: [] }])`), buildPreNormalizationPriceConstraintsFromData returns `{}` (lines 1896-1922 leave `query` empty, and `priceListIds` is undefined for this path). `priceService_.list({}, ...)` then loads every price in the table with its price_rules. The old code only loaded prices for the price sets named in the input. This is a performance regression on the path the PR is meant to speed up, and it is triggered by an empty prices array, which is valid input.
